 Revenue from operations rises to ₹43,875 crore in Q2FY27, while first-half profit nearly doubles year-on-year
 Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reported a 57 per cent rise in net profit to ₹15,488.64 crore in Q2FY27, aided by higher oil and gas realisations. (Photo: Reuters)
 PTI New Delhi 1 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 11:41 PM IST Listen to This Article
 State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) on Thursday reported a 57 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit for the September quarter, driven by higher oil and gas realisations despite largely flat production.   Net profit of Rs 15,488.64 crore in July-September - the second quarter of the current 2026-27 fiscal year - compared with Rs 9,847.97 crore earnings in the same period a year back, according to a stock exchange filing by the company.   The profit was, however, lower than Rs 17,033.81 crore in the preceding April-June quarter.   Revenue from operations rose to Rs 43,875.15 crore in the second quarter from Rs 33,030.56 crore a year back.     For the first half, ONGC reported a net profit of Rs 32,522.45 crore, almost double the Rs 17,872.20 crore of April-June 2025.
